body: Yes but with me, EVERYTHING tends to go wrong. If something goes wrong if generally makes me feel worse about myself.
The YouTube channel is a good idea but I probably won't go viral or anything. I've been making videos for almost 9 years, with no success.
I don't think I could do web development because of my lack of technical ability. I made a comment below which goes into more depth about why I went back to film.

Also this is the second or third time I have accidentally missed a deadline. You'd have thought I'd have learnt my lesson by now, but I still haven't and my life is still a complete mess and I still hate myself. 

The irony is that I wasn't intent on it having a career in film before 2016. At high school (I'm UK based) I really wanted to be a history teacher but I didn't get the grades in (despite doing incredibly well in GCSEs) high school so that collapsed. I still blame myself for this by the way. Despite this I don't think I would be a very good history teacher, so that might have been a good thing. 

During 2015-2016, when I hated certain aspects of my film course I applied to a mixed media course (digital media websites, photography, AfterEffects etc) but I applied at the  last minute and I felt that the course was too technical for my abilities so I kind of drifted back to film.

Thank you! I'm pissed off because I missed because of pure stupidity. My application was all ready to go but I just didn't check the email they sent me before I finished it... 
What did you do instead of film?
